markers.description: Homonym number (represented by Roman numerals like II., III.).
Variant form (e.g., alternate spellings or dialects like DUM'-E).
English usage note (e.g., context, 'Trop.', 'Spoken of rain', or literal constraints).
English translation of the vernacular example.
Cross-reference to another lexeme (e.g., 'See Däbä', derivations, or root references).

rules: Homographs are differentiated using Roman numerals immediately following the headword, mapping to \hm.
Numbered senses use Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3...) mapped to \sn, preceding the usage note or gloss.
Variant forms (\va) follow the main headword and may have their own part of speech.
Derivations (Der.) and 'See' pointers are treated as cross-references (\cf), often specifying the target's part of speech.
Examples are grouped in bundles: an italicized vernacular sentence (\xv) followed by its italicized English translation (\xe).
Usage notes (\ue) often clarify the context or subject of the verb (e.g., 'With inua.', 'Trop.') and appear before the gloss or among examples.
